headlines.text: Wall Street slides at midday Wednesday (Dow -1.2% to ~50,130, S&P 500 -0.6% to ~7,293, Nasdaq -0.35% to ~24,244) as Nvidia's beat-and-raise quarter fails to lift shares and traders await Fed minutes and Anthropic's IPO pricing
Target's Q3 comparable sales jump 5.6% (vs. ~3.6% est.) with EPS of $2.65 as turnaround accelerates; shares climb premarket and full-year guidance raised

Fed's Oct. 27-28 meeting minutes due out this afternoon (2pm ET), expected to detail the 10-2 vote to hold rates at 3.75%-4%, with Cook and Hammack's dissents favoring a hike underscoring little room for a December cut
Anthropic set to price its IPO Wednesday evening at $70-$78 a share, valuing the AI firm near $1.4 trillion ahead of Thursday's Nasdaq debut under ticker ANT
Nvidia shares slip despite blowout Q3 (revenue $115.8B, +103% YoY, topping ~$109B est.) as investors digest interim CEO Colette Kress's rocky first earnings call since Jensen Huang's exit
Lowe's Q3 sales jump 9.3% (comps +1.8%) with adjusted EPS of $3.10, a sixth straight quarter of positive comps under CEO Marvin Ellison; shares surge ~6% premarket and full-year outlook raised
